title: Phenology drives asymmetric responses of ecosystem productivity stability to warming and cooling
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Ecosystem productivity stability is a key indicator of ecosystem functioning under climate change, but the role of cooling periods in increasingly variable climates remains poorly resolved. Using a 17-year reciprocal transplant experiment along an elevational gradient in alpine grasslands, we examined the asymmetric effects of temperature fluctuations, including warming and cooling, on the above-ground net primary productivity (ANPP) temporal stability. Warming significantly decreased ANPP temporal stability, whereas cooling had no net effect. These asymmetric responses were primarily governed by phenological dynamics. The decline in ANPP temporal stability under warming was primarily driven by advanced leaf-out phenology. Under cooling, delayed leaf-out and reduced plant size promoted temporal stability of ANPP, but these effects were offset by direct cooling-induced suppression and delayed flowering. Our findings indicate that periods of cooling are unlikely to mitigate instability driven by warming, highlighting the necessity to incorporate temperature asymmetry and phenological regulation into predictions of ecosystem stability under increasing climate variability.

摘要

生态系统生产力稳定性是气候变化背景下评估生态系统功能状态的重要指标，而在当前持续加剧的气候波动进程中，降温阶段的作用机制仍缺乏系统性认知。 本研究依托沿海拔梯度建立、持续17年的高寒草地双向移栽实验，系统探究了增温和降温过程的温度波动对地上净初级生产力 (above-ground net primary productivity, ANPP) 时间稳定性的非对称影响。 研究结果表明，增温显著降低了ANPP的时间稳定性，而降温并未对其产生显著净效应。这种非对称响应主要由物候动态过程主导。增温条件下，ANPP时间稳定性的下降主要由返青期的显著提前驱动；而在降温条件下，虽然返青期推迟和植株个体小型化有助于提高ANPP时间稳定性，但该正效应被降温的直接生理抑制作用以及开花期推迟带来的负效应所抵消。 由此可见，降温过程难以抵消增温导致的生态系统稳定性下降。这一结果提示，在气候波动持续增加背景下开展生态系统稳定性预测时，需将温度变化的非对称效应及其物候调控机制纳入核心分析框架。
